rows.text: The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput under varying sequence lengths. To establish a reliable benchmark, the test utilizes a fixed KV cache size to isolate decoding latency. This benchmark measures tokens per second (TPS) across multiple GPU configurations. A primary benchmark metric involves the memory bandwidth utilization during the decoding phase. In this benchmark, the attention mechanism's overhead is quantified relative to the total compute budget. Each benchmark iteration employs a standardized prompt to ensure consistency. The benchmark results indicate that B70 performance scales linearly with batch size until memory saturation. Consequently, the benchmark highlights the critical bottleneck of memory-bound operations in large-scale decoding. A rigorous benchmark must account for kernel fusion efficiency. Therefore, this benchmark serves as a baseline for optimizing inference engines. Final benchmark analysis suggests that quantization significantly improves the benchmark score for throughput-constrained environments.
